overall: The AG found the Commission violated the Open Meeting Law by omitting the meeting location's street address from its March 30 notice, but found it harmless and not intentional, so no relief was ordered.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Commission's March 30 meeting notice was not specific enough because it omitted the street address of the meeting location.
allegations.key_passage: For the reasons stated in that determination, we find that the Commission violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the notice omission was intentional. The AG found the error was harmless because no member of the public was confused, so no relief was ordered.
allegations.key_passage: because the complaint does not allege that any member of the public was confused by the meeting notice at issue, we find that this error was harmless.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the notice omission was an intentional violation of the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: because the Commission had not yet received our office's determination at the time of the March 30 meeting notice posting, and thus was unaware of the relief ordered at that time, we find that this violation was not intentional.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
